esde.label: ES-DE
esde.note: System folders use the ES-DE names.

knulli.label: Knulli
knulli.note: Card root is the SHARE partition (/userdata). Folder names are case-sensitive and use Batocera system names; Knulli only scans subfolders of roms/. Systems with knulli = null have no Knulli system.

onion.label: Onion
onion.note: Miyoo Mini family (SigmaStar SSD202D) running Onion. Card root is the FAT32 SD card; Onion creates missing Roms/ folders on first install. Folder names are case sensitive, differ from the stock Miyoo card, and are not ES-DE or Batocera names. Subfolders work only one level deep (e.g. Roms/GB/Hacks). The discs of multi-disc games go in a hidden .multi-disc subfolder with the .m3u beside it, so the list shows each game once. BIOS files go in the root BIOS/ folder unless a system says otherwise. Systems with onion = null have no verified Onion folder. Source: https://onionui.github.io/docs/emulators/folders

allium.label: Allium
allium.note: Miyoo Mini family (SigmaStar SSD202D) running Allium, which uses the Onion card layout and matches systems by file extension first, so the folders are the same as Onion's. Allium reads a gamelist.xml (path, name, image, rating, releasedate, developer, publisher, genre) in each ROM folder and finds box art in Imgs/. Sources: https://github.com/goweiwen/Allium/wiki/2.-Add-your-Games!, https://github.com/goweiwen/Allium

spruce.label: Spruce
spruce.note: Miyoo Mini family (SigmaStar SSD202D), Miyoo Flip (RK3566) and Miyoo A30 (Allwinner A33) running spruceOS. Card root is the FAT32 SD card. System folders are the upper-case spruce names (SFC for the SNES, MD for the Genesis, FC for the NES, PS for the PlayStation), and ROMs go straight into them. Spruce reads a miyoogamelist.xml (name only) in each ROM folder and QOI box art from Imgs/, Imgs_med/ and Imgs_small/ (PNG or JPG there makes PyUI prompt to convert). BIOS files go in the root BIOS/ folder, keeping the libretro subfolders (dc/, nds/, neocd/, ...). Systems with spruce = null have no spruce folder. Sources: https://github.com/spruceUI/spruceOS/wiki/11.-Adding-Games, https://github.com/spruceUI/spruceOS/wiki/10.-Adding-BIOS

muos.label: muOS
muos.note: MustardOS 2606.0 on Anbernic H700 handhelds (and the RG Vita Pro). Card root is the games partition (exFAT or FAT32). muOS matches folder names to systems ignoring case, spaces, hyphens, underscores and plus signs, so the names here are the Knulli ones where muOS knows them. Systems with muos = null have no muOS system. Sources: https://muos.dev/docs/infrastructure/storage, https://muos.dev/installation/catalogue

emudeck.label: EmuDeck
emudeck.note: EmuDeck on the Steam Deck and Steam Machine (SteamOS). Card root holds Emulation/; emulators install to the internal SSD. System folders use the ES-DE names, except Wii U, Xbox 360 and Model 2, which keep their ROMs in a roms/ subfolder. BIOS files go in Emulation/bios, with subfolders only where an emulator expects one. Source: https://emudeck.github.io/cheat-sheet/

rocknix.label: ROCKNIX
rocknix.note: ROCKNIX (Linux handheld firmware). Card root is the games partition; ROMs live in roms/<system>/, BIOS files in roms/bios/. RetroArch saves sit next to the ROM and states go in roms/savestates/<system>. Folder names are ROCKNIX's own (e.g. coleco, sgfx, pico-8). Systems with rocknix = null have no ROCKNIX folder on the card. Source: https://github.com/ROCKNIX/distribution

nextui.label: NextUI
nextui.note: MinUI-style card (Anbernic RG SP and similar) running NextUI. Card root is the SD card. System folders are named "<Name> (TAG)": the tag in parentheses picks the emulator, and BIOS files go in Bios/<tag>/. Systems beyond the base install need NextUI's Extras zip. Systems with nextui = null have no NextUI tag. Source: https://nextui.loveretro.games/getting-started/roms/
